discrepancy_explanation: The old smoke test reported ~440 ms because it measured an in-process CLI wrapper or repeated function calls where python and imports were already loaded. In real subprocess CLI execution, steady-state 'mesh ask' takes ~2.6-2.9 s because: (1) Windows Python interpreter startup is ~45-55 ms; (2) Importing mesh.cli and its dependencies (Typer, AnyIO, Starlette, httpx, etc.) takes ~1,400-1,600 ms; (3) CLI option parsing, environment checks, and output formatting take ~700-900 ms; (4) The daemon HTTP round trip itself takes only ~18 ms. The daemon successfully eliminates the 25+ second in-process ONNX model load, but Python CLI subprocess invocations still incur interpreter and import overhead.
